annotations.title: One ratio as a series (daily for valuation)

description: Return one ratio as a series, most recent first. For a valuation ratio (market_cap, enterprise_value, pe_ttm, ps_ttm, pb, ev_ebitda_ttm, ev_ebit_ttm, fcf_yield, dividend_yield) there is one point per trading session: the IEX close of that day times the standardized facts known that evening (trailing twelve months for flows, the latest balance sheet), so a P/E series never uses a filing accepted later. Points are withheld after a split-sized move until split data exists; data.price_basis says which listing was used and why a company is not priced (several share classes such as BRK-A and BRK-B, an ADR, no prices). Each point is a value object whose proof.inputs lists the close first, then the facts; proof_get recomputes it. For a fundamentals ratio (gross_margin, roe, nii_to_avg_loans_securities...) there is one point per fiscal period of period_type. IEX is a single venue and its last trade is not the official close; say so when quoting. Use it for the history of one ratio, such as a P/E series or a margin trend.

as_of.description: Knowledge date or timestamp (YYYY-MM-DD or RFC 3339). The answer is what FinancialMD knew at that instant: only facts whose known interval contains as_of. Omit for the current view.

company.description: Company identifier: a FinancialMD id ("fmd_01H..."), an SEC CIK ("cik:320193"), or a ticker ("ticker:AAPL", optionally with the MIC "ticker:AAPL.XNAS"). A bare ticker like "AAPL" is accepted and sent as ticker:AAPL. An issuer on an EU or UK regulated market that does not file with the SEC has no CIK: pass its LEI ("lei:IOG4E947OATN0KJYSD45") or its fmd_ id.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from a previous page (data.next_cursor).

from.description: Valuation only: first session date, inclusive (YYYY-MM-DD).

limit.description: Maximum number of periods or items to return (default 30, at most 1000).

period_type.description: Period basis: annual (fiscal years), quarterly, ltm (last twelve months) or ytd (year to date).

ratio_id.description: Ratio id. Valuation ids give a daily series; the others one point per period.

ticker.description: Valuation only: the listing whose close is used (default the primary listing with bars).

to.description: Valuation only: last session date, inclusive (YYYY-MM-DD).

name: ratios_daily

outputSchema.description: The FinancialMD envelope (docs/API.md section 2): data plus meta (request_id, as_of knowledge time, matched company, coverage, pipeline_version, licence, terms, proof_base). Every numeric value inside data is an object with value, unit, currency, period, known interval, restated flag, method and a proof pointing at the filing. On failure the result is isError with an error object instead.

data.description: { ratio_id, label, formula, metric_format, period_type ("daily" for valuation), view, items: [value objects], next_cursor, price_basis?: { listing, source, unavailable } }

error.description: Present only on isError results: the API error code and message plus remedy hints.

meta.description: Request metadata: request_id, as_of, company resolution, coverage, pipeline_version, licence, terms, proof_base.

attribution.description: Citations a source requires on anything shown from the answer.

title: One ratio as a series (daily for valuation)
